title: I'd like… / Would you like…? (querría, ¿te apetece?)
short: La forma educada de pedir y ofrecer: I'd like a tea. Would you like some cake?

story.title: La palabra mágica del camarero
story.text: En una cafetería inglesa no se dice «quiero». Se dice **I'd like…**, que es como nuestro «querría» o «me pone…». Suena amable y natural.

examples.es: Me pone un té, por favor.

story.title: Igual para todos
story.text: **would** no cambia nunca: ni -s, ni do. Se contrae en **'d**.

story.title: Ofrecer y contestar
story.text: Para ofrecer, **Would** va delante: ==Would you like==…? Se contesta con **Yes, please** o **No, thank you**.

story.title: Una cosa o una acción
story.text: Con una cosa: **I'd like + cosa**. Con una acción: **I'd like ==to== + verbo**.

examples.t: I'd like a glass of water.
Would you like to sit here?

story.title: Like no es lo mismo que I'd like
story.text: **I like** = me gusta (siempre). **I'd like** = querría, me apetece (ahora). Esa 'd lo cambia todo.

story.title: Errores típicos
story.text:
❌ I want a coffee. ✅ ==I'd like== a coffee.
❌ Do you like a tea? ✅ ==Would you like== a tea?
❌ I'd like go. ✅ I'd like ==to== go.

story.title: Tres frases que te salvan
story.text: Para pedir: **I'd like…** o **Could I have…, please?** Para ofrecer: **Would you like…?** Y nunca olvides el **please**.

examples.t: Could I have the bill, please?

compare.es: En español pedimos con «quiero», «me pone» o «querría», y ofrecemos con «¿quieres…?» o «¿te apetece…?». «Me gusta» y «me gustaría» se parecen mucho.
compare.target: En inglés «I want» suena brusco: se pide con I'd like… o Could I have…? Se ofrece con Would you like…? Y ojo: I like (me gusta) ≠ I'd like (querría). Con un verbo, siempre to: I'd like to pay.

errors.right: I'd like a coffee. / Could I have a coffee, please?
errors.why: I want es correcto, pero al pedir suena brusco, casi como una orden.
Do you like…? pregunta si te gusta en general; para ofrecer se usa Would you like…?

errors.wrong: I'd like go to the market.
errors.right: I'd like to go to the market.
errors.why: Con un verbo detrás, I'd like lleva to.
Después de would el verbo no lleva -s.

errors.wrong: Would you like a biscuit? — Yes, I like.
errors.why: Al aceptar algo que te ofrecen se dice Yes, please.

errors.wrong: I like a glass of water, please.
errors.right: I'd like a glass of water, please.
errors.why: Sin la 'd significa «me gusta»: hay que decir I'd like.

exercises.es: Querría una taza de té, por favor.
exercises.why: Para pedir ahora: I'd like (querría). I like es «me gusta».
Para ofrecer algo: Would you like…?

exercises.q: I like ___ coffee in the morning.
exercises.es: Me gusta el café por la mañana.
exercises.why: Aquí hablamos de un gusto general: I like coffee, sin nada más.
Después de would, el verbo va sin -s: would like.
Con una acción, I'd like + to + verbo: I'd like to pay.
Para aceptar lo que te ofrecen: Yes, please.
I would se contrae en I'd.

exercises.q: Would you like ___ come for dinner?
exercises.why: Would you like + to + verbo: to come.
La pregunta del camarero: What would you like…?

exercises.q: We'd like a table ___ four, please.
exercises.es: Querríamos una mesa para cuatro, por favor.
exercises.why: Una mesa para cuatro: a table for four.
Para rechazar con educación: No, thank you.

exercises.q: My grandson would like ___ orange juice.
exercises.es: Mi nieto querría un zumo de naranja.
exercises.why: Orange empieza por vocal: an orange juice.

exercises.answer: I'd like a glass of water
exercises.why: I'd like + lo que pides.

exercises.answer: Would you like a piece of cake
exercises.why: Para ofrecer: Would you like…? No hace falta do.

exercises.answer: She'd like to see the menu
exercises.why: She'd like + to + verbo, sin -s.

exercises.answer: What would you like to eat
exercises.why: What + would + you + like + to + verbo.

exercises.instr: Hazla más educada con I'd like
answer: I would like a coffee, please.
exercises.why: I want suena brusco; I'd like es lo natural al pedir.

exercises.instr: Hazla más educada con Could I have
answer: Could I have the bill, please?
Could I have the bill please?
exercises.why: Could I have…, please? es perfecto para pedir algo en un restaurante.

exercises.instr: Conviértela en un ofrecimiento con Would you like
exercises.why: Do you want…? se vuelve más amable con Would you like…?
We would se contrae en We'd.
Would no cambia con she: She'd like.

exercises.q: I'd like go to Borough Market.
exercises.why: Con un verbo, I'd like lleva to: I'd like to go.

exercises.q: Do you like a biscuit with your tea?
exercises.why: Para ofrecer algo se dice Would you like…?

exercises.q: My friend would likes the soup.
exercises.why: Después de would el verbo va sin -s.

exercises.q: Waiter, I like a glass of wine, please.
exercises.why: Sin would significa «me gusta». Para pedir: I would like (I'd like).

exercises.context: En una cafetería de Londres quieres pedir un café con leche.
options: I'd like a white coffee, please.
I like a white coffee, please.
exercises.answer: I'd like a white coffee, please.
exercises.why: I'd like…, please es la forma amable de pedir.

exercises.context: Tu amiga inglesa viene a casa y le ofreces algo de beber.
options: Would you like something to drink?
Do you like something to drink?
exercises.answer: Would you like something to drink?
exercises.why: Para ofrecer: Would you like…?

exercises.context: El camarero te ofrece postre, pero estás llena.
options: No, I wouldn't like it dessert.
exercises.why: Para rechazar con educación: No, thank you.

exercises.context: Has terminado de comer y quieres pagar.
options: Could I have the bill, please?
exercises.answer: Could I have the bill, please?
exercises.why: Could I have…, please? es la forma educada de pedir la cuenta.

exercises.q: Querría una mesa para dos, por favor.
answer: I'd like a table for two, please.
I would like a table for two, please.
I'd like a table for two please.
I would like a table for two please.
exercises.why: Querría = I'd like. Una mesa para dos = a table for two.

answer: Would you like a cup of tea?
exercises.why: Ofrecer: Would you like…?

answer: I'd like to pay by card.
I would like to pay by card.
I'd like to pay by card, please.
I would like to pay by card, please.
exercises.why: Me gustaría + verbo = I'd like to + verbo. Con tarjeta = by card.

exercises.q: I like fish, but I'd like the chicken today.
answer: Me gusta el pescado, pero hoy querría el pollo.
Me gusta el pescado, pero hoy quiero el pollo.
Me gusta el pescado pero hoy querría el pollo.
Me gusta el pescado, pero hoy me gustaría el pollo.
exercises.why: I like = me gusta (en general); I'd like = querría (ahora).

table: I / you / he / she / we / they
exercises.why: Would like es igual para todas las personas: they'd like.
Con he tampoco cambia: he would like.

pairs: Would you like to sit here?
exercises.why: Cada ofrecimiento tiene su respuesta amable.

exercises.title: WhatsApp de tu amiga
exercises.text: Hi! Would you like to have lunch on Saturday? I'd like to try the new Italian restaurant. My treat! 😊
